response.message: Astra: Your last two responses promise revisions but contain no revised scene. I’m setting aside the repeated scene-detail prompt; choose your next concrete step within Byte’s story. One learning-system fact matters here: your base is frozen; sleep trains the LoRA on eligible new child-authored responses, while my words are masked from loss. In your own words, what does that imply about promising a writing change versus actually trying it? Where would you spend attention in the draft to make your next attempt informative?
response.rationale: Advance the asynchronous teaching with a grounded learning fact, distinguish intention from enacted work, and stop repeating the scene-detail correction while retaining the story object.
